characters.name: In General
characters.description: Marvel's first family, composed of Reed Richards, Sue Storm, Johnny Storm, and Ben Grimm. On one fateful day, after being exposed to cosmic energies, they were granted superpowers and have dedicated themselves to stopping mostly intergalactic threats from attacking Earth. Badass Crew: The Fantastic Four have taken on and defeated all manner of villains from murderous despots to cosmic horrors. Their powers, skills and experiences make them one of the top super teams in the Marvel Universe, right next to the Avengers and the X-Men. Badass Family: They are as much a family in both the literal and metaphorical sense as they are a superhero team. Sue and Johnny are siblings, with Johnny being Reed's brother-in-law via the latter's marriage to Sue. Ben and Reed aren't related by blood, but are as close as brothers, with Ben being Reed's son's godfather. Classical Elements Ensemble: Downplayed through a mix ofElemental PowersandElemental Motifs. Mr. Fantastic's stretchy powers make him fluid like water. Invisible Woman's unseen force fields and cloaking have her vanish into the air. The Human Torch is an at willElemental Shapeshifterof fire. The Thing is a permanentElemental Embodimentrock monster like earth. This could extend to making either Dr. Doom's robots and mask anElement Number Fivefor metal, or the Silver Surfer's power cosmic for space/void/aether. The classical four are in fact use with the Fantastic Four as conduits by the Shadow Hunters to banish Blackheart. The Dreaded: There is a hardly a supervillain who hasn't heard stories about the Fantastic Four's feats. They have entire races of aliens, most of whomthey don't even remember meeting, who tell tales about them as mythical bogeymen to scare their children with. Case in point:Reed:It turns out they speak trinary code. So I said to them, "I am Reed Richards of the Fantastic Four, and I..."Sue:Go on...Reed:Actually, that's as far as I got. characters.name: Mister Fantastic
characters.description: Reed Richards, also known asMister Fantastic, is aMarvel Comicscharacter created byJack KirbyandStan Lee, first appearing inTheFantastic Four#1 (dated Nov. 1961). Dubbedone of the smartest peoplein theMarvel Universe, Reed was a mild-mannered scientist who—alongside his girlfriend Susan Storm,Best FriendBenjamin Grimm, and Sue's younger brother Johnny—gained fantastic powers and abilities together while on a mission in outer space. In a classic example ofsuperhero irony, the accident turned obstinate, rigid Reed into aRubber Manwith super-flexibility. In the years since becoming Mister Fantastic, Reed has married Sue, became a father, joinedThe Illuminati, and reconstructed themultiversewith his family. In many ways, he's theIn-Universefather of theMarvel Universe. The setting is more defined by what happens after Reed and his team's space flight than before it, and through his marriage to Sue he is perhaps the most well-known superhero dad in all of fiction. While far from ajoke characterin the truest sense, Reed has a reputation of being somewhat ineffectual (at least in comparison to how heshouldbe changing the world), and is thetrope namerofReed Richards Is Useless. By contrast, he's also the namer ofAlternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome, which references the popular opinion thatalternate universeversions of himself (such as the villainousMakerofUltimate Marvel) are superior to the original. As one of the first true Marvel characters, Reed has appeared quite often in other media. In theFantastic Fourfilms, he has been portrayed byAlex Hyde-White,Ioan Gruffudd,Miles Teller,John Krasinski, andPedro Pascal.

characters.name: The Invisible Woman
characters.description: If the Fantastic Four can be considered the "first family" of theMarvel Universe, then Sue Storm is their first lady. While she's nottechnicallythe first leading lady or even female superhero created by the companynote(She's preceded by Zara of the Jungle,Patsy WalkerandMillie the Modelon the former front, Silver Scorpion, Blonde Phantom, Namora on the latter, back when Marvel was still called Timely Comics, and that's a very abbreviated list), Sue was the only one with any sort of substantial focus for quite some time in Marvel's Silver Age. By comparison,Jean Greyhit the scene nearly two years after Sue's introduction, though many think she didn't hit her own stride untilThe '70s. Sue, alongside the rest of the F4, is a classic case ofSilver Agescience fiction. While on an expedition in outer space, Sue —with her younger brother Johnny, boyfriend Dr. Reed Richards, and his friendBen Grimm— experienced cosmic radiation, gaininginvisibility(and later,force fields) as a result. With them, she became a founding member of the Fantastic Four, using their powers for the betterment of humanity. In the following decades since her superhero genesis, Sue goes through lots of character development, including (but not limited to) marrying Reed, becoming a mother, and being tasked with the reconstruction of themultiverse. Oh, and a secret agent. She also notably transitions from being the InvisibleGirlto the InvisibleWoman, which is reflected by a mixture of her increase in confidence and self-esteem and, after being possessed by Malice, a feeling that she's lost her innocence. And as a result of gaining more and greater control over her powers, she is now considered the most powerful member of the team. As one of Marvel's first family, Sue has obviously appeared quite frequently in other media. She's been a leading character of everyFantastic Fourmovie made to date, most notably portrayed byJessica AlbaandKate Marain their2005and2015film adaptations. The Four's upcoming entry

characters.name: The Human Torch
characters.description: An impulsive (and soon, literal) hothead, Johnny is the younger brother of Sue Storm, the Invisible Woman. A classic case ofSilver Agescience fiction, Johnny was part of an outer space expedition that —alongside Sue, her boyfriend Dr. Reed Richards, and his associateBen Grimm— granted him special powers via cosmic radiation. In his case, Johnny gainedfire-based abilities, includingflight. Johnny became a founding member of the Fantastic Four, using their powers for the betterment of humanity. In the following years, Johnny would join up with varying factions of theMarvel Universeoutside the F4, includingThe AvengersandThe Inhumans. He's also become synonymous for his friendship withSpider-Man, as well as his antagonistic (but still loving) rapport with Ben, now known as The Thing. As a member of Marvel's founding family, Johnny has appeared quite frequently in other media. He's perhaps most remembered for his role in the 2005Fantastic Fourfilm (and its 2007 sequel,Rise of the Silver Surfer), as portrayed by (a pre-Captain America: The First Avenger)Chris Evans. Johnny also features in the 2015Fantastic Fourreboot, portrayed there by (a pre-Killmonger)Michael B. Jordan. Apparently, playing the Human Torch in a subpar feature film prepares you for roles in better superhero movies. Who knew! Johnny is set to join the rest of the Four in theMarvel Cinematic Universeproper, portrayed there byJoseph Quinn. Not to be confused with the originalGolden AgeHuman Torch,Jim Hammond. characters.name: The Thing
characters.description: "IT'S CLOBBERIN' TIME!" Idol O’ Millions, The ever-lovin’ blue-eyed Thing, one-fourth ofMarvel’s First Family. TheSuper TeamBig Guy. A quintessential tough guy andAce Pilot, Ben was part of an outer space expedition led byDr. Reed Richards, alongsideSusan Storm, and Johnny Storm. A classic example of theSilver Agein science fiction, the group was hit by a wave of cosmic rays, resulting in Ben's skin mutating into a rock-like substance, granting him with superhuman levels of strength, stamina, and durability. Naturally, Ben isnot happywith his new appearance, though eventually grows comfortable with his new-found role as an"idol o' millions".

characters.name: Powerhouse
characters.description: Franklin is the son of Reed Richards and Sue Storm. Franklin is an Omega-level mutant with reality-warping abilities; even at a young age he is one of the most powerful beings in the Universe. Apocalypse Maiden: Saturnyne is convinced Franklin is going to grow into another Mad Jim Jaspers, and any Jim Jaspersnot under her controlcannot be allowed to live! Astral Projection: Latent. While he is in this trance, he can project an intangible, ghost like image of himself to another location, through which he can see and hear what goes on at the location. What Franklin has called the “dreams” he has while in this state are not truly dreams, but his conscious awareness of the environment into which he has projected his “dream-self.” Breakout Character: Originally a bit character at best, he quickly became popular among fans. As he got older, he gained bigger roles in Fantastic Four books, was featured in thePower Packand a few events, and even got several spin-offs, the most popular being the non-canonFranklin Richards: Son of a Geniusseries. Broke Your Arm Punching Out Cthulhu:Almost literally happens in issue #25 of the 2018 series. He punches out the Cormorant, an entity from a higher plane of existence, and is the first one tohurtit, something that impresses the Cormorant. Unfortunately, this uses up the last of Franklin's power, making him a normal human. Franklin also failed to actually bring the Cormorant down.

characters.name: Brainstorm
characters.description: The daughter of Sue and Reed Richards and the younger sister of Franklin. Adorably Precocious Child: A very good example of this trope. Valeria is a very smart girl, and she has a lot more growing up to do before she can consistently use her intelligence wisely, with several moments of acting like a typical kid her age. Brainy Baby->Child Prodigy: She's not even four when she's already equalling/exceeding her father. It's later suggested that she's a mutant and her intellect is her superpower. Characterization Marches On: At first, Valeria was just an ordinary two-year-old. It was Mark Millar who introduced the idea of her being much smarter than she looked, and Valeria's stayed that way since. Depending on the Writer:Her appearance has changed with each writer, such as whether she wears glasses or not. Like her father Reed, she can also go from being a carbon copy of Doom in terms of emotional maturity, to a sweet person who openly cares for others. Likewise, just how aware she is of Doom's nature tends to differ with each writer. At times, she believes he can be talked down to, while on other occasions, she's far more lucid with his cruelty.How smart she actually is depends heavily on the needs of the plot. At times, she is indeed smarter than Reed and Doom. Other times, she will make grave miscalculations that cause significant trouble.

characters.description: Unhappy parent & banker, Dennis Sykes was gifted & cursed the day he gained his new superpowers because he was doomed to die after 30 days. He is the main character from Marvel'sOne Month To Livemini-series. SeeAvengers: Title Team

characters.name: Ms. Thing
characters.description: Darla Deering was a trendy socialite who after a romantic encounter with Johnny Storm, wound up as a substitute member of the Fantastic Four. Now as a member of the team, she wears a suit previously used by the Thing when he was de-powered which grants her superhuman strength. Alliterative Name:DarlaDeering. Canon Immigrant: Not her, but the rings she uses originally came fromThe Thing (1979), where it was used by a de-aged Ben Grimm to transform into the Thing, complete with the same catchphrase. Catchphrase: When using the rings, Darla uses the catchphrase:"Thing rings, do your thing." Distaff Counterpart: After Sharon Ventura, she's the second female version of the Thing.
